claim: Harbor 0.24.0 was installed through its documented uv tool route into a private tool directory and ran its own hello-world example task through the Docker environment: one zero-spend oracle trial and one claude-code trial (claude-haiku-5-5, Anthropic API key injected per command by the repository credential runner). Both trials ended with reward 1.0 and 0 exceptions. One TCP connect from a throwaway container to the local gateway port at the gvisor-tap-vsock gateway address timed out, so container-resident adapters have no measured route to the gateway.
limitations: One trial of Harbor's trivial hello-world task with one adapter (claude-code) on one route (Anthropic API). Route b (an OpenAI-compatible base URL) and the other seven adapters in the route table were read from source and have no live result.
The Claude Code CLI inside the container was the latest at run time (2.1.296) because the adapter installs latest unless --ak version= is given; the agent CLI is not pinned by this receipt.

The upstream mirror head dc933be7 is 31 commits after v0.24.0 and was not installed. The installed artifact is the v0.24.0 wheel; the source files cited for the route table are identical between the wheel and the mirror head except installed/base.py, codex.py, mini_swe_agent.py, environments/docker/docker.py and cli/jobs.py.

Container-to-gateway reachability was measured once: one TCP connect from a throwaway ubuntu:24.04 container on the default bridge network to 10.0.2.1:21128 timed out after 5 s (silently dropped, not refused) while a control connect to 10.0.2.1:53 opened. The probe covers one image, one network path and one port; it does not test other addresses, compose networks or a changed daemon configuration.
Agent setup took 171.34 s of the 204.17 s trial on a bare ubuntu:24.04 image. No prebuilt-image run was measured.

Isolation from <HOME>/.claude was checked by modification time and size plus a construction argument. A live Claude Code session and sibling agents rewrite <HOME>/.claude.json and <HOME>/.claude/projects continuously, so those two before/after values do not discriminate on their own.

The docker container count moved from 67 to 66 during the smoke window. No container named for Harbor, hello-world or hb__ existed before or after; the change is attributed to a process outside this lane.

The terminus-2 --ak api_base= gateway route (the model client runs in the Harbor process on the host) is source-read, not live-tested: no request reached the gateway through it. Only the eight named adapters and terminus-2 were read for where their model client runs; terminus-2 is the only host-side client found among them, and the other 36 registered adapters were not read for this.

The container-to-gateway timeout is measured, but its cause is read from source (rootlesskit v3.1.0 and the daemon's observed --disable-host-loopback flag); it was not tested by changing the flag, which is host configuration.

The smoke trial's four named phases sum to 184.51 s of its 204.17 s; the other 19.66 s is measured in three windows (data.smoke.trial) and attributed from source to log sync, trajectory conversion, artifact collection and environment teardown, without timing those sub-steps.

harbor_run_environment.env_shim_disclosure: Every harbor invocation ran through a short environment shim kept only in the scratch tree: it exports HOME, DOCKER_HOST and TMPDIR, sets HARBOR_TELEMETRY=off, changes to the scratch working directory and execs harbor. It contains no Harbor logic and is never committed. The CC accepted it on 2026-10-12 as a disclosed, scratch-only isolation measure.

route_b_probe.ruling: CC 2026-10-12: one probe from a throwaway ubuntu:24.04 container from the local image, no pull, no change to the Docker daemon or its rootlesskit flags.
route_b_probe.network: default bridge network of the rootless daemon (container default gateway 172.17.0.1), the same tap0 egress as Harbor's compose networks

probe.result: not open: the connect timed out and was silently dropped; no refusal was received

route_b_probe.cause_source: rootless-containers/rootlesskit v3.1.0 (tag object 4fab82caf726318cef33bf82912546b8a529eaab, commit 62d2101fbbe4f79bc845a337c4e868d27ff602c9), pkg/network/gvisortapvsock/gvisortapvsock.go:106-124 (gateway is the network base plus 1, 10.0.2.1) and 142-148 (NAT from 10.0.2.1 to host 127.0.0.1 is configured only when --disable-host-loopback is absent)
route_b_probe.cause_status: The timeout is measured. Its cause is read from the rootlesskit source and the daemon's observed flag; it was not tested by changing the flag (host configuration).
route_b_probe.route_policy_ruled: Gateway routes in the comparison use terminus-2 with --ak api_base= (the model client runs in the Harbor process on the host; source-read, not live-tested); container adapters use route a only until a measured route exists.

oracle_dry_run.purpose: Harbor's own oracle agent runs the task's reference solution through the same Docker environment and verifier as the live smoke; no model call and no key.

trial.name: hello-world__8NxiCZF
trial.unattributed_attribution: Windows measured from the trial's own timestamps. By source for this shared-verifier task (harbor/trial/single_step.py:40-54, trial/trial.py:551-556 and 1052-1058, agents/installed/claude_code.py:1657-1669, environments/docker/docker.py:1208), the middle window holds the agent-output sync (log download and the claude-code trajectory conversion on the host), the agent-log upload and artifact collection, and the last window holds the environment teardown after the verifier (docker compose down --rmi local --volumes --remove-orphans), with finished_at stamped afterwards. Sub-steps inside each window were not timed.

smoke.timestamp_note: The job-level result.json started_at and finished_at are naive local time (13:09:59 to 13:13:23); trial-level phase fields are UTC with a Z suffix. This receipt cites the trial fields and the date -u run meta.

unpublished_originals.disclosure: Kept in the lane's private scratch tree and not published. No digest of any of them is published: the repository is public, and a digest of unsanitized run output, a transcript or a home-state snapshot would let a guessed path or name be confirmed offline (correction #161). The data block of this receipt is the published projection of their measured values; the resolved-distribution list is published as resolved-distributions.txt and the adapter matrix as the decision record's table.
